Tranche ferme : APS et APD, DIA, relevés-vérifications complémentaires, étude comparative de deux scénarios, étude d'approvisionnement énergétique, CSSI, assistance à l'établissement des dossiers de subvention ; elle se conclut par la fixation du coût prévisionnel des travaux et du forfait définitif de rémunération. title: Q301--Biodesix, Inc. (621 II) (PENDING PROPOSAL)
description: Revised Language SCOPE OF SOLICITATION The Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program is also known as the GSA Schedules Program or the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Program. The FSS program is directed and managed by GSA and provides Federal agencies with a simplified process for obtaining commercial supplies and services at prices associated with volume buying. Indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity contracts are awarded to provide supplies and services at stated prices for given periods of time. GSA has delegated authority to the VA to manage the Schedules for medical supplies under the VA FSS program. This solicitation is for the offering of reference laboratory services for the purpose of providing medical laboratory testing for the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition and to assess patient health to make clinical decisions for patient care.� This solicitation is not for facilities that only collect and/or prepare specimens nor for those facilities that only serve as a mailing service and do not perform testing services. This solicitation is issued to establish contracts which may be used on a nonmandatory basis by eligible users, as a source of supply for the supplies or services described herein, for domestic. Domestic delivery is defined as delivery within the 48 contiguous states, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington, DC, and U.S. territories . Offerors may be limited to geographic service areas based upon licensing requirements or may offer nationwide delivery. This solicitation further requires that offered prices cover delivery to destinations (i.e. F.O.B. destination) located within the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia. Offerors can choose whether or not prices cover delivery f.o.b. destination to Alaska, Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Additionally, the solicitation defines the number of calendar days after receipt of order (ARO) within which delivery must be made. Offerors who cannot provide the required minimum geographic coverage, that is one state, will not be considered for award. As specified in the solicitation, offerors shall comply with all state, federal and local regulations, licenses, permits, and accreditation necessary to manage and conduct preanalytic specimen testing services. Offerors must comply with states that require out of state licenses/permits. Therefore, laboratories conducting clinical testing on specimens originating in a state that requires an out of state license/permit must hold that state s Department of Health (or other governing body) clinical laboratory permit, licenses, etc. � Offerors that are not compliant with the originating state s licensing and/or permit requirement, regardless of location, will not be considered for an award for that specific state. Offerors may not subcontract to another laboratory to circumvent the originating state s requirement for licensing, permits, etc. The offeror, in itself, is required to meet the requirements of the solicitation without the aid of a subcontractor. The Government retains sole discretion to determine the offeror s capability, compliance, and to limit SINs or geographic coverage. Commercial Items Per GSA regulations at 538.271(a), MAS awards are for commercial items as defined in FAR 2.101. Special Item Numbers (SINs): FSS solicitations set forth broad categories of accepted products/services, referred to as Special Item Numbers (SINs), listed in the Continuation of SF1449 in Vendor Response Document 02. Offerors are not required to submit their entire catalog of products/services but are free to choose which items they will offer as long as those items fall within one of the solicitation s pre-defined SIN categories. Items that do not fall within one of these SINs are considered to be out of scope of the solicitation and cannot be awarded. An item s acceptability under the schedule may be further restricted by a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. Offered diagnostic testing services must be categorized under the accepted services referenced under the Special Item Numbers (SINs) and classified as a specialties or subspecialties of tests as defined under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA). Please note that items offered are further restricted to those tests with CPT codes. Additionally, FSS will not award any home diagnostic tests under this schedule. Home diagnostic tests/test kits may be proposed under Schedule 65 V II Invitro Diagnostics, Reagents, Test Kits and Test Sets. FDA Regulatory Requirements Reagents used to perform the tests must be FDA cleared, as appropriate, or be identified as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT). Offerors of tests not in compliance with these requirements shall not be considered for award under this solicitation. New Items vs. Refurbished or Grey Market Goods This solicitation is for the award of new items only. The Contractor shall provide only new equipment and new parts for the required products described herein. Absolutely no grey market goods or refurbished products shall be provided under any delivery order. Grey market goods are defined as genuine branded goods sold outside of an authorized sales-territory (or by non-authorized dealers in an authorized territory) at prices lower than being charged in authorized sales territories (or by authorized dealers). All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer s warranty. Trade Agreements Act The Trade Agreements Act is applicable to all Schedules. In exercising its authority under FAR Part 25, Foreign Acquisition, purchases by Ordering Activities are restricted to either U.S.-made or designated country end products as defined in clause FAR 52.225-5. For the purposes of this services schedule, origin is determined by the country in which the firm providing the service is established, not the location at which the services are performed. Notice of Additional Requirements - Ordering Level In addition to the terms and conditions set forth in this solicitation, the contractor may, in the performance of orders issued under this contract, be responsible for further requirements at the ordering level. For more information on these potential, additional requirements, please see the note in Solicitation Document 01 after FAR clause 52.216-18 Ordering. Please note that the VA does not promote the use of any company s specific Schedule contract. Vendors should be aware that obtaining a VA Schedule contract is not a guarantee of sales. Vendors awarded a VA Schedule contract will need to market their supplies and services to Government customers as they would to commercial customers. A listing of eligible schedule users can be found at on GSA s website at http://gsa.federalschedules.com/resources/eligible-gsa-schedule-users/. description: *** 11/16/2026: AMENDMENT 07 ISSUED - SEE SUMMARY OF AMENDMENT AT BOTTOM OF POSTING*** ***SUMMARY ONLY - SEE ATTACHED COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION DOCUMENT FOR FULL DETAIL*** APS _ Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Brief: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Commercial Items Agile Professional Services ("APS�) Department of the Army Project Name: Agile Professional Services ("APS") Solicitation Number: W900KK-26-R-A023 NAICS Code: 541990 (All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services) Set-Aside: Total Small Business Set-Aside Contract Type: Labor Hours/T&M 1. General Information This combined synopsis/solicitation is issued by Army Contracting Command - APG - Orlando Division to procure Agile Professional Services ("APS"). The acquisition is structured to support critical technical and professional operations under a flexible framework, to be proposed and developed by the successful offeror. Key acquisition parameters include: � Set-Aside Status: 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. � Small Business Size Standard: $19.5M, or as defined by SBA regulations. � Primary NAICS Classification: 541990 � All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services. � Contract Vehicle Type: Labor Hours/T&M 2. Solicitation Details This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. This combined synopsis/solicitation is prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular FAC 2025-06, effective August 27, 2025.and DFARS Publication Notice (DPN) July 2, 2026. As described in the attached FAR 52.212-2, The Army will adopt aspects of FAR Part 15 evaluation procedures. Considering the novel, and commercial, nature of these services this is deemed necessary to balance fairness, transparency, and competition with the interests of expediency and flexibility 3. Description of Requirement CPE ST3 has a need for Agile Professional Services (APS) support services to provide the organization with the ability to augment its Military and Government Civilian workforce in order to execute its mission. The services will be limited to providing professional support services, under a Performance Based Services model, to CPE ST3 and CPE ST3 customers for limited requirements which are related to CPE ST3�s mission. Since its inception, CPE ST3 has relied on contractor support to conduct its mission in all phases of life cycle management due to insufficient personnel within the organization to successfully perform the required services. This model of a Government footprint with a scalable contractor workforce has enabled CPE ST3 to be very flexible and agile in its mission to support the changing needs of the Army. The services to be performed will include related activities in support of all aspects of providing responsive integrated and interoperable infrastructure for simulation, training, testing, and threat solutions. APS support services are required for effective, efficient, and responsive full lifecycle management of efforts to include, but not limited to: vision statements and doctrine, development of architectures, program support (e.g., acquisition and budget planning, business and financial programming and execution, modeling, simulation, simulator, training device, and instrumentation development, documentation, fielding and execution, system analysis and integration, integrated logistics support, strategic planning, contingency and mission support, security cooperation/international relations, program oversight, independent verification validation and test evaluation, prototype development, sustainment and operations, and analysis of emerging technologies support), and subject matter experts on military tactics, techniques, and procedures. Potential areas of growth are envisioned but not limited to be in the areas of Cyber and Information Warfare, Robotics, Unmanned Vehicles, Home Station Training, Multi-Sensory Simulation, Artificial Intelligence, Hypersonics, Directed Energy, Electronic Warfare, Autonomous Systems, Multi-Domain Integration, Target and Threat Systems, Environment Modeling, Human Performance Training, Security Cooperation, Nuclear Engineering, and Medical Training. The critical performance requirement is the successful development and transition of CPE ST3 from a traditional, staffing-based support model to a task-based, outcome-driven Agile delivery framework that is to be developed by the Performer. Success will be measured by the contractor's ability to develop and iterate, through performance under the resultant contract, a framework that both provides the following, and is able to be replicated across future requirements. 4. Primary Government sites include Orlando, FL, and Redstone Arsenal, AL (including 24/7 operations). Additional Government sites include: Fort Campbell, KY; Fort Hood, TX; Fort Drum, NY; Fort Irwin, CA; Fort Polk, LA; Fort Rucker, AL; Fort Bragg, NC; Hohenfels, Germany; and Camp Humphreys, South Korea. 5. Applicable FAR Provisions/Provisions: See Attachment 7. The provisions and clauses apply to this acquisition and are incorporated by reference or full text as applicable. The full text of the FAR and DFARS clauses may be accessed electronically at https://www.acquisition.gov/. 6. DoD SAFE Link Upon issuance of Phase II Notification / Invitation, the Government will be issuing each respective Offeror (2) DoD SAFE links. Links will be sent to the POC identified in the Phase I Cover Letter: DoD SAFE Link #1 - Pick Up - JIRA Data: Each Offeror will receive an email from DoD SAFE with a link in which to download all the JIRA Data and Instructions. title: RFP-797-FSS-04-0001-R3: 621II Medical Laboratory Testing & Analysis Services
description: Revised Language SCOPE OF SOLICITATION The Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program is also known as the GSA Schedules Program or the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Program. The FSS program is directed and managed by GSA and provides Federal agencies with a simplified process for obtaining commercial supplies and services at prices associated with volume buying. Indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity contracts are awarded to provide supplies and services at stated prices for given periods of time. GSA has delegated authority to the VA to manage the Schedules for medical supplies under the VA FSS program. This solicitation is for the offering of reference laboratory services for the purpose of providing medical laboratory testing for the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition and to assess patient health to make clinical decisions for patient care.� This solicitation is not for facilities that only collect and/or prepare specimens nor for those facilities that only serve as a mailing service and do not perform testing services. This solicitation is issued to establish contracts which may be used on a nonmandatory basis by eligible users, as a source of supply for the supplies or services described herein, for domestic. Domestic delivery is defined as delivery within the 48 contiguous states, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington, DC, and U.S. territories . Offerors may be limited to geographic service areas based upon licensing requirements or may offer nationwide delivery. This solicitation further requires that offered prices cover delivery to destinations (i.e. F.O.B. destination) located within the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia. Offerors can choose whether or not prices cover delivery f.o.b. destination to Alaska, Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Additionally, the solicitation defines the number of calendar days after receipt of order (ARO) within which delivery must be made. Offerors who cannot provide the required minimum geographic coverage, that is one state, will not be considered for award. As specified in the solicitation, offerors shall comply with all state, federal and local regulations, licenses, permits, and accreditation necessary to manage and conduct preanalytic specimen testing services. Offerors must comply with states that require out of state licenses/permits. Therefore, laboratories conducting clinical testing on specimens originating in a state that requires an out of state license/permit must hold that state s Department of Health (or other governing body) clinical laboratory permit, licenses, etc. � Offerors that are not compliant with the originating state s licensing and/or permit requirement, regardless of location, will not be considered for an award for that specific state. Offerors may not subcontract to another laboratory to circumvent the originating state s requirement for licensing, permits, etc. The offeror, in itself, is required to meet the requirements of the solicitation without the aid of a subcontractor. The Government retains sole discretion to determine the offeror s capability, compliance, and to limit SINs or geographic coverage. Commercial Items Per GSA regulations at 538.271(a), MAS awards are for commercial items as defined in FAR 2.101. Special Item Numbers (SINs): FSS solicitations set forth broad categories of accepted products/services, referred to as Special Item Numbers (SINs), listed in the Continuation of SF1449 in Vendor Response Document 02. Offerors are not required to submit their entire catalog of products/services but are free to choose which items they will offer as long as those items fall within one of the solicitation s pre-defined SIN categories. Items that do not fall within one of these SINs are considered to be out of scope of the solicitation and cannot be awarded. An item s acceptability under the schedule may be further restricted by a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. Offered diagnostic testing services must be categorized under the accepted services referenced under the Special Item Numbers (SINs) and classified as a specialties or subspecialties of tests as defined under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA). Please note that items offered are further restricted to those tests with CPT codes. Additionally, FSS will not award any home diagnostic tests under this schedule. Home diagnostic tests/test kits may be proposed under Schedule 65 V II Invitro Diagnostics, Reagents, Test Kits and Test Sets. FDA Regulatory Requirements Reagents used to perform the tests must be FDA cleared, as appropriate, or be identified as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT). Offerors of tests not in compliance with these requirements shall not be considered for award under this solicitation. New Items vs. Refurbished or Grey Market Goods This solicitation is for the award of new items only. The Contractor shall provide only new equipment and new parts for the required products described herein. Absolutely no grey market goods or refurbished products shall be provided under any delivery order. Grey market goods are defined as genuine branded goods sold outside of an authorized sales-territory (or by non-authorized dealers in an authorized territory) at prices lower than being charged in authorized sales territories (or by authorized dealers). All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer s warranty. Trade Agreements Act The Trade Agreements Act is applicable to all Schedules. In exercising its authority under FAR Part 25, Foreign Acquisition, purchases by Ordering Activities are restricted to either U.S.-made or designated country end products as defined in clause FAR 52.225-5. For the purposes of this services schedule, origin is determined by the country in which the firm providing the service is established, not the location at which the services are performed. Notice of Additional Requirements - Ordering Level In addition to the terms and conditions set forth in this solicitation, the contractor may, in the performance of orders issued under this contract, be responsible for further requirements at the ordering level. For more information on these potential, additional requirements, please see the note in Solicitation Document 01 after FAR clause 52.216-18 Ordering. Please note that the VA does not promote the use of any company s specific Schedule contract. Vendors should be aware that obtaining a VA Schedule contract is not a guarantee of sales. Vendors awarded a VA Schedule contract will need to market their supplies and services to Government customers as they would to commercial customers. A listing of eligible schedule users can be found at on GSA s website at http://gsa.federalschedules.com/resources/eligible-gsa-schedule-users/. title: 6515--FY27 SENTEC CO 2 MONITORS-SLEEP CLINIC
description: Special Notice Special Notice Page 3 of 3 Special Notice *= Required Field Special Notice Page 1 of 3 The Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 8, hereby provides notice of its intent to award a sole-source, fixed, The VA Medical Center requires the acquisition of Sentec tCOM Transcutaneous CO Monitoring Systems, including V Sign sensors, mounting hardware, PSG adapter cables, and extended warranties, to support continuous noninvasive CO and oxygenation monitoring in the Sleep Lab for diagnostic polysomnography. These devices are required to meet clinical standards for assessing sleep disordered breathing and PAP titration studies. The V-Sign Sensor is a non-invasive patient sensor used to continuously measure transcutaneous carbon dioxide (TcCO ) and oxygen saturation. This monitoring capability is essential for diagnosing and managing patients with sleep-disordered breathing and respiratory insufficiency. The Sentec V-Sign Sensor is a proprietary component manufactured exclusively for use with the Sentec TcCO monitoring system. The sensor is fully compatible with the VA s existing equipment, including integration with the Polysmith system, pre-loaded adult modes, and customized display configurations. No other manufacturer produces a sensor that is technically compatible or validated for use with the Sentec TcCO monitor. Use of an alternative sensor would require replacement of the entire monitoring system, resulting in unnecessary cost, operational disruption, and potential risk to patient care. The associated NAICS code for this procurement is 334510. The vendor will be Sentec AG, 40 Albion Road, Suite 100, Lincoln, RI 02865. A firm-fixed-price purchase order is anticipated. It is the Government s belief that only the proposed source possesses the required capabilities to successfully meet this requirement. It is the Government s intention to solicit and negotiate with only this source. A Sole Source Justification has been prepared. The delivery requirement is requested 90 days ARO. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes or proposals. It is not a solicitation or request for offers. No solicitation package is available. title: Q702--Santa Maria IOTA
description: Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Health Administration Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) October 13, 2026 PRESOLICITATION NOTICE Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation Services in support of the Santa Maria, CA OPC 100% SDVOSB SET ASIDE This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice that the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) intends to solicit quotes to provide non-personal Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation (IOT&A) services for the Santa Maria Outpatient Clinic (OPC). This requirement supports VHA's mission by providing contractor support services to help bring the hospital into full planned operations that will provide health care services to Veterans. This will be a firm-fixed-price contract with an estimated Period of Performance of 31-months. VHA authorized a 28,656 net usable square foot (NUSF) outpatient clinic (OPC) lease project in Santa Maria, California. The project will support the parent facility, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System. The new OPC will replace the existing clinic in Santa Maria, which currently contains 28,612 NUSF. The new clinic will be able to accommodate future workload, provide ample parking (200 spaces), and will adequately support all services in a modern, efficient space. The new clinic will provide all the services offered at the existing clinic, including Primary Care, Mental Health, Audiology, Eye Clinic, Dental, Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, Pathology and Blood Draw, Logistics, Telehealth, Business Office, Community Engagement and Reintegration, and Women's Health. This new facility is essential to accommodate the current demand of 6,634 Unique Santa Maria Veterans and the future potential demand of 7,500 Santa Maria catchment Enrollees The scope includes project support for planning, activating, outfitting, and transitioning the staff and Veterans/patients associated with the project. The scope of services includes Comprehensive Project Management, Comprehensive Interior Design, FF&E, and Space Planning Support; CONOPS and Transitioning Planning; Acquisition Support Services to include package development, Activation, Delivery, Relocation and Installation, Training, and Turnover and Post Occupancy Support for the identified project. This requirement will be set-aside 100% for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) using FAR Part 12 and 37. To be eligible for an SDVOSB set aside under VA s Veterans First Contracting Program, SDVOSBs must: be verified by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as SDVOSB (see https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ for details) and meet the small business size standard for NAICS 541614. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted on Contract Opportunities for download on or about 30 October 2026. Anticipated closing date of the solicitation will be 30 November 2026. Solicitation initial posting date and the closing date are subject to change as necessary. title: RFP-797-FSS-04-0001-R3: 621II Medical Laboratory Testing & Analysis Services
description: Revised Language SCOPE OF SOLICITATION The Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program is also known as the GSA Schedules Program or the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Program. The FSS program is directed and managed by GSA and provides Federal agencies with a simplified process for obtaining commercial supplies and services at prices associated with volume buying. Indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity contracts are awarded to provide supplies and services at stated prices for given periods of time. GSA has delegated authority to the VA to manage the Schedules for medical supplies under the VA FSS program. This solicitation is for the offering of reference laboratory services for the purpose of providing medical laboratory testing for the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition and to assess patient health to make clinical decisions for patient care.� This solicitation is not for facilities that only collect and/or prepare specimens nor for those facilities that only serve as a mailing service and do not perform testing services. This solicitation is issued to establish contracts which may be used on a nonmandatory basis by eligible users, as a source of supply for the supplies or services described herein, for domestic. Domestic delivery is defined as delivery within the 48 contiguous states, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington, DC, and U.S. territories . Offerors may be limited to geographic service areas based upon licensing requirements or may offer nationwide delivery. This solicitation further requires that offered prices cover delivery to destinations (i.e. F.O.B. destination) located within the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia. Offerors can choose whether or not prices cover delivery f.o.b. destination to Alaska, Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Additionally, the solicitation defines the number of calendar days after receipt of order (ARO) within which delivery must be made. Offerors who cannot provide the required minimum geographic coverage, that is one state, will not be considered for award. As specified in the solicitation, offerors shall comply with all state, federal and local regulations, licenses, permits, and accreditation necessary to manage and conduct preanalytic specimen testing services. Offerors must comply with states that require out of state licenses/permits. Therefore, laboratories conducting clinical testing on specimens originating in a state that requires an out of state license/permit must hold that state s Department of Health (or other governing body) clinical laboratory permit, licenses, etc. � Offerors that are not compliant with the originating state s licensing and/or permit requirement, regardless of location, will not be considered for an award for that specific state. Offerors may not subcontract to another laboratory to circumvent the originating state s requirement for licensing, permits, etc. The offeror, in itself, is required to meet the requirements of the solicitation without the aid of a subcontractor. The Government retains sole discretion to determine the offeror s capability, compliance, and to limit SINs or geographic coverage. title: FY27 Scott AFB Air Show Narrator
description: Scott Air Force Base is in need of a Narrator for upcoming Air Show in June of 2027. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, transportation, communications capability, and other items and services necessary to perform Airshow Narrator services for the 2027 Scott AFB Airshow, except for Government-furnished property and services specifically identified in this Performance Work Statement (PWS). The Contractor shall provide an experienced and currently qualified Airshow Narrator to support safe, professional, timely, and engaging presentation of the Airshow in accordance with AFMAN 10-1004, Conducting Air Force Open Houses; approved installation plans; the approved flying schedule; the applicable mishap/emergency-response plan; and local Scott AFB procedures. The Airshow Narrator shall narrate the airshow and keep spectators informed of ongoing and upcoming events, approved sponsor recognition, activities, entertainment, concessions, public service announcements, safety information, and other Government-approved messages. The Contractor shall coordinate directly with the Government-designated Airshow Director, Contracting Officer's Representative (COR), Air Operations Officer, Air Boss, Ground Boss, public affairs personnel, emergency-response agencies, performers, sound-support contractor, and other agencies designated by the Government. The Contractor shall not issue aviation-control instructions, direct emergency responders, make unapproved public statements, or modify Government-approved emergency language. The Contractor shall promptly communicate approved emergency, safety, weather, schedule, evacuation, shelter, accountability, and crowd-control messages when directed by the Government-designated responsible person or in accordance with the approved emergency plan. The Contractor shall attend, either in person or virtually, all required 2027 Scott AFB Airshow planning meetings with Scott AFB Airshow staff. At a minimum, the Contractor shall attend four monthly planning meetings, or fewer if coordinated with Scott AFB Airshow staff. The Contractor may be required to attend additional meetings and shall attend those meetings virtually unless otherwise directed by the Government. All required in-person meetings, designated site visits, travel, and associated expenses shall be included in the Contractor's price proposal, except for Government-furnished lodging and transportation identified in this PWS. The Airshow Narrator shall be on site for the Airshow rehearsal on 11 June 2027 and for the 2027 Scott AFB Airshow on 12 and 13 June 2027. Additionally, the Airshow Narrator shall be available on site during the week of the Airshow to support approved promotions, media engagements, planning meetings, performer coordination, sound checks, and other Airshow-related requirements as directed by the Government. Specific event times for all dates will be determined and provided by the Government. The Contractor shall provide all services described in this PWS at Scott AFB, provided weather, installation conditions, safety requirements, and operational requirements permit performance. Please reference the PWS attachement.

title: Wharton Research Data Services (WRDS) Renewal
description: INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE Wharton Research Data Services products (WRDS) #SS-OFR-27-006 The Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC), on behalf of the Office of Financial Research (OFR) and the Financial Stability Oversight Council (FSOC), intends to contract with Trustees of the University of Pennsylvania, 3451 Walnut St Ste 440A, Philadelphia, PA 19104-6205, on a sole source basis. There is no competitive vendor or regulatory agency that provides these datasets. The proposed Contractor developed and owns the propriety and patented hardware, software and algorithms that are used in these products and support the services specifically required for this acquisition; thereby, the proposed source has the sole unique technical and other resources required for this acquisition. Pursuant to its mandate, the OFR/FSOC has a need for access to business, financial, economic, and marketing data through a self-managed service with centralized access; a high volume of cross-disciplinary data; and flexibility of delivery including computing cloud access. With this data, the OFR/FSOC also requires technical and research technical, and research specialists available for online assistance and orientation toward academic research information furnished on a platform which consolidates access to major datasets and databases used by academia, regulatory agencies, and commercial entities with financial market and economic information requirements to meet these needs, the OFR/FSOC is pursuing Wharton Research Data Services (WRDS) access. WRDS consolidates access through one platform to commonly accessed financial data sets such as FactSet Revere, S&P CUSIP, Hedge Fund Research, and others. WRDS is the only known platform which creates single point access to commercial datasets such as CUSIP, MF Links, CRSP and other baseline financial data. This expedites research and crisis response as multiple portals need not be consulted to perform the necessary due diligence. OFR needs to purchase WRDS to obtain regulatory and original source financial data and integrate it with information from baseline financial commercial datasets in order to effectively fulfill its mission of anticipating systemic threats to the financial system and publishing the studies found in its Financial Monitor. Much of the source data is not readily obtainable from other sources in its original form nor from a single point of access. The source data and ease of access enable the OFR to respond to critical emergent analytical requests more readily within the financial services sector. Integrating data from different sources and possessing a single point of access for it allows for new insights that may be critical in understanding fast-moving market developments during times of crisis. Whilst regulatory data collections implicitly define data standards these implicit standards do not always envision the benefits of integration with other (commercial) sources. These challenges have a significant impact on the ability to quickly perform research and analysis across multiple datasets. description: � Alertus Software Licensing and Support Martinsburg VA Medical Center Notice ID: 36C24527Q0081 Issuing office: Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office 5 Response deadline: November 30, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time Point of contact: Bernie Trotter; bernadine.trotter@va.gov Purpose The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is conducting market research to identify capable sources for software licensing and support of the existing Alertus emergency notification system at the Martinsburg VA Medical Center. VA seeks responses from the manufacturer and from distributors, resellers, and other service providers that can furnish the required licensing and support, directly or through a documented arrangement. VA welcomes responses from all capable sources, including SBA-certified service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses (SDVOSBs) and veteran-owned small businesses (VOSBs). Anticipated requirement VA anticipates a firm-fixed-price requirement with one 12-month base period and four 12-month option periods. The place of performance is the Martinsburg VA Medical Center, 510 Butler Avenue, Martinsburg, WV 25405. No hardware supplies are anticipated. The anticipated scope includes: Providing software licenses, updates, security patches, troubleshooting, diagnosis, configuration, and software repairs for the existing Alertus system. Maintaining the installed software at the most current version approved under the VA Technical Reference Model (TRM) and applying patches in accordance with applicable federal and VA security requirements. Accepting trouble calls 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and responding to and completing software repairs within 48 hours of receiving a trouble call, unless an alternate timeframe is coordinated with and accepted by the Contracting Officer s Representative under the resulting contract or order. Maintaining Alertus as a device option within the existing AtHOC Mass Notification System and preserving emergency notification capability through existing text-to-voice beacons, speakers, and public-address interfaces. Meeting applicable VA information security, privacy, and Section 508 accessibility requirements identified in the draft Statement of Work. Information requested Submit a concise capability statement addressing the following: Company information. Provide your legal business name, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), point of contact, email address, business size, and any applicable SBA certifications, including SDVOSB or VOSB status. Licensing and authorization. Explain how your firm would furnish the required Alertus licenses, updates, and security patches. If relying on a manufacturer, distributor, or reseller arrangement, identify the arrangement and explain what it covers. If readily available, provide a current authorization letter or other documentation showing the scope of that arrangement. Support and integration. Explain how your firm would provide 24/7 trouble-call intake, meet the 48-hour response and repair requirement, and maintain the existing AtHOC and public-address integrations. Identify which work your firm would perform directly, which work would be performed by Alertus or another partner, and any exceptions to the stated requirements. Deployment and maintenance. State whether your firm supports VA-hosted deployments, vendor-hosted deployments, or both. Distinguish support for the Alertus application from maintenance of the host server and operating system. This notice does not request a hosting migration. Contract vehicle and budgetary information. If the licenses and support are available under an existing federal contract vehicle, identify the vehicle, your contract number, and which items or services are currently available under it. If readily available, provide nonbinding budgetary pricing or the principal pricing assumptions for the base and option periods. A formal quotation is not requested. Submission instructions and disclaimer Email responses to Bernadine.trotter@va.gov by November 30, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time. Use the Subject line: 36C24527Q0081 Alertus Licensing and Support RFI. Clearly mark any proprietary information and do not include patient information, credentials, or sensitive system details. This notice is issued for market research and acquisition planning only. It is not a solicitation, a request for quotations or proposals, or a notice of intent to award sole source. Responses are not offers and cannot be accepted to form a binding contract. VA will not reimburse response preparation costs. This notice does not commit VA to issue a solicitation, use a particular contract vehicle, or make an award.� �

description: Revised Language SCOPE OF SOLICITATION The Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program is also known as the GSA Schedules Program or the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Program. The FSS program is directed and managed by GSA and provides Federal agencies with a simplified process for obtaining commercial supplies and services at prices associated with volume buying. Indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity contracts are awarded to provide supplies and services at stated prices for given periods of time. GSA has delegated authority to the VA to manage the Schedules for medical supplies under the VA FSS program. This solicitation is for the offering of reference laboratory services for the purpose of providing medical laboratory testing for the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition and to assess patient health to make clinical decisions for patient care.� This solicitation is not for facilities that only collect and/or prepare specimens nor for those facilities that only serve as a mailing service and do not perform testing services. This solicitation is issued to establish contracts which may be used on a nonmandatory basis by eligible users, as a source of supply for the supplies or services described herein, for domestic. Domestic delivery is defined as delivery within the 48 contiguous states, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington, DC, and U.S. territories . Offerors may be limited to geographic service areas based upon licensing requirements or may offer nationwide delivery. This solicitation further requires that offered prices cover delivery to destinations (i.e. F.O.B. destination) located within the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia. Offerors can choose whether or not prices cover delivery f.o.b. destination to Alaska, Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Additionally, the solicitation defines the number of calendar days after receipt of order (ARO) within which delivery must be made. Offerors who cannot provide the required minimum geographic coverage, that is one state, will not be considered for award. As specified in the solicitation, offerors shall comply with all state, federal and local regulations, licenses, permits, and accreditation necessary to manage and conduct preanalytic specimen testing services. Offerors must comply with states that require out of state licenses/permits. Therefore, laboratories conducting clinical testing on specimens originating in a state that requires an out of state license/permit must hold that state s Department of Health (or other governing body) clinical laboratory permit, licenses, etc. � Offerors that are not compliant with the originating state s licensing and/or permit requirement, regardless of location, will not be considered for an award for that specific state. Offerors may not subcontract to another laboratory to circumvent the originating state s requirement for licensing, permits, etc. The offeror, in itself, is required to meet the requirements of the solicitation without the aid of a subcontractor. The Government retains sole discretion to determine the offeror s capability, compliance, and to limit SINs or geographic coverage. Commercial Items Per GSA regulations at 538.271(a), MAS awards are for commercial items as defined in FAR 2.101. Special Item Numbers (SINs): FSS solicitations set forth broad categories of accepted products/services, referred to as Special Item Numbers (SINs), listed in the Continuation of SF1449 in Vendor Response Document 02. Offerors are not required to submit their entire catalog of products/services but are free to choose which items they will offer as long as those items fall within one of the solicitation s pre-defined SIN categories. Items that do not fall within one of these SINs are considered to be out of scope of the solicitation and cannot be awarded. An item s acceptability under the schedule may be further restricted by a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. Offered diagnostic testing services must be categorized under the accepted services referenced under the Special Item Numbers (SINs) and classified as a specialties or subspecialties of tests as defined under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA). Please note that items offered are further restricted to those tests with CPT codes. Additionally, FSS will not award any home diagnostic tests under this schedule. Home diagnostic tests/test kits may be proposed under Schedule 65 V II Invitro Diagnostics, Reagents, Test Kits and Test Sets. FDA Regulatory Requirements Reagents used to perform the tests must be FDA cleared, as appropriate, or be identified as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT). Offerors of tests not in compliance with these requirements shall not be considered for award under this solicitation. New Items vs. Refurbished or Grey Market Goods This solicitation is for the award of new items only. The Contractor shall provide only new equipment and new parts for the required products described herein. Absolutely no grey market goods or refurbished products shall be provided under any delivery order. Grey market goods are defined as genuine branded goods sold outside of an authorized sales-territory (or by non-authorized dealers in an authorized territory) at prices lower than being charged in authorized sales territories (or by authorized dealers). All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer s warranty. Trade Agreements Act The Trade Agreements Act is applicable to all Schedules. In exercising its authority under FAR Part 25, Foreign Acquisition, purchases by Ordering Activities are restricted to either U.S.-made or designated country end products as defined in clause FAR 52.225-5. For the purposes of this services schedule, origin is determined by the country in which the firm providing the service is established, not the location at which the services are performed. Notice of Additional Requirements - Ordering Level In addition to the terms and conditions set forth in this solicitation, the contractor may, in the performance of orders issued under this contract, be responsible for further requirements at the ordering level. For more information on these potential, additional requirements, please see the note in Solicitation Document 01 after FAR clause 52.216-18 Ordering. Please note that the VA does not promote the use of any company s specific Schedule contract. Vendors should be aware that obtaining a VA Schedule contract is not a guarantee of sales. Vendors awarded a VA Schedule contract will need to market their supplies and services to Government customers as they would to commercial customers. A listing of eligible schedule users can be found at on GSA s website at http://gsa.federalschedules.com/resources/eligible-gsa-schedule-users/. Current contract holders do not need to complete sections below: GEOGRAPHIC COVERAGE Current Coverage: List the specific U.S. states, including Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington D.C., and U.S. territories in which you are currently providing or have provided services relative to this solicitation in the last two years. Enter Nationwide if currently/recently providing nationwide (i.e. domestic delivery) coverage. Proposed Coverage: Offerors may propose to provide service to individual states or nationwide. Respond to each question below regarding proposed coverage. For each choice selected, you must also check the box to verify your submission of the requested supporting documentation. Please note that qualifying supporting documentation means evidence of compliance with all federal, state and local license and certification in accordance with Statement of Work, Section II General Qualifications and Sub-Factor B.1 Organization sub-paragraph (a)(b) - Organizational and Professional Staff. description: ***ONLY SEAPORT MAC HOLDERS ARE ELIGIBLE FOR THIS OPPORTUNITY.*** This is a combined Sources Sought/Advance Notice only. The Naval Surface Warfare Center Dahlgren Division (NSWCDD) Gun and Electric Weapon Systems (E Department) has a follow-on requirement for support across multiple effectors, ammunition and weapons systems. See the attached Advance Notice/Sources Sought for additional information. NSWCDD will host an in-person Industry Day regarding the anticipated follow-on contract for Gun Weapon Systems (GWS), on 19 November 2026 at the University of Mary Washington-Dahlgren Campus, 4224 University Drive, King George, VA 22485, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM EST with a start time of 9:00 AM EST. To support market research under RFO Part 10, NSWCDD will offer optional one-on-one sessions with industry partners who request it. Requests for one-on-one sessions should be made along with interested parties registrations and are planned to occur from 12:00 PM to 5:00 PM on 19 November 2026 upon the conclusion of the Industry Day Question and Answer period. In the event more requests are received than can be accommodated on the afternoon of 19 November 2026, a separate meeting date will be coordinated. Requests for optional one-on-one meetings will not be honored after the registration deadline of 12:00 PM (Noon) EST 18 November 2026. Virtual one-on-one sessions will not be held. This notice is issued for informational and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. The Government is not requesting proposals at this time. Participation in the Industry Day is voluntary and is not required in order to compete for any future solicitation.

title: Request for Information - Contract Writing System Recompete
description: Request for Information Contract Writing System Recompete 2099AC27N00004 RFI-DO-27-002 The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to identify capable vendors and commercially available solutions that can support the U.S. Department of the Treasury requirements for a contract writing system as part of the Contract Writing System Recompete. The Government seeks information regarding vendors� technical capabilities, available products and services, hosting, system functionality, integration, and ability to satisfy the attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements. Interested vendors should review the entire Technical Exhibit and identify capabilities, limitations, and potential alternatives. This RFI is solely for market research and acquisition planning and is not a solicitation. This is an RFI for market research purposes, and not a solicitation. 1. SCOPE SUMMARY (See attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements) The Department of the Treasury is conducting market research to identify qualified vendors capable of providing an enterprise contract writing system solution to support Treasury acquisition and procurement operations. Technical Exhibit 1 identifies anticipated functional, technical, operational, security, hosting, integration, and support requirements designated as Mandatory or Value Added. The Government may use information obtained through this RFI to refine requirements and determine an appropriate acquisition strategy for any future solicitation. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to gather information from interested vendors regarding their capabilities and potential solutions for a Contract Writing System to support the Department of the Treasury's acquisition and contracting requirements. The incumbent contractor providing the Department's existing Contract Writing System is Unison Software, Inc. II. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE The anticipated period of performance for any resulting contract has not been finalized. Additional information regarding the period of performance, implementation schedule, and other acquisition details may be provided in a future solicitation, should one be issued. III. description: Revised Language SCOPE OF SOLICITATION The Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program is also known as the GSA Schedules Program or the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Program. The FSS program is directed and managed by GSA and provides Federal agencies with a simplified process for obtaining commercial supplies and services at prices associated with volume buying. Indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity contracts are awarded to provide supplies and services at stated prices for given periods of time. GSA has delegated authority to the VA to manage the Schedules for medical supplies under the VA FSS program. This solicitation is for the offering of reference laboratory services for the purpose of providing medical laboratory testing for the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition and to assess patient health to make clinical decisions for patient care.� This solicitation is not for facilities that only collect and/or prepare specimens nor for those facilities that only serve as a mailing service and do not perform testing services. This solicitation is issued to establish contracts which may be used on a nonmandatory basis by eligible users, as a source of supply for the supplies or services described herein, for domestic. Domestic delivery is defined as delivery within the 48 contiguous states, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington, DC, and U.S. territories . Offerors may be limited to geographic service areas based upon licensing requirements or may offer nationwide delivery. This solicitation further requires that offered prices cover delivery to destinations (i.e. F.O.B. destination) located within the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia. Offerors can choose whether or not prices cover delivery f.o.b. destination to Alaska, Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Additionally, the solicitation defines the number of calendar days after receipt of order (ARO) within which delivery must be made. Offerors who cannot provide the required minimum geographic coverage, that is one state, will not be considered for award. As specified in the solicitation, offerors shall comply with all state, federal and local regulations, licenses, permits, and accreditation necessary to manage and conduct preanalytic specimen testing services. Offerors must comply with states that require out of state licenses/permits. Therefore, laboratories conducting clinical testing on specimens originating in a state that requires an out of state license/permit must hold that state s Department of Health (or other governing body) clinical laboratory permit, licenses, etc. � Offerors that are not compliant with the originating state s licensing and/or permit requirement, regardless of location, will not be considered for an award for that specific state. Offerors may not subcontract to another laboratory to circumvent the originating state s requirement for licensing, permits, etc. The offeror, in itself, is required to meet the requirements of the solicitation without the aid of a subcontractor. The Government retains sole discretion to determine the offeror s capability, compliance, and to limit SINs or geographic coverage. Commercial Items Per GSA regulations at 538.271(a), MAS awards are for commercial items as defined in FAR 2.101. Special Item Numbers (SINs): FSS solicitations set forth broad categories of accepted products/services, referred to as Special Item Numbers (SINs), listed in the Continuation of SF1449 in Vendor Response Document 02. Offerors are not required to submit their entire catalog of products/services but are free to choose which items they will offer as long as those items fall within one of the solicitation s pre-defined SIN categories. Items that do not fall within one of these SINs are considered to be out of scope of the solicitation and cannot be awarded. An item s acceptability under the schedule may be further restricted by a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. Offered diagnostic testing services must be categorized under the accepted services referenced under the Special Item Numbers (SINs) and classified as a specialties or subspecialties of tests as defined under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA). Please note that items offered are further restricted to those tests with CPT codes. Additionally, FSS will not award any home diagnostic tests under this schedule. Home diagnostic tests/test kits may be proposed under Schedule 65 V II Invitro Diagnostics, Reagents, Test Kits and Test Sets. FDA Regulatory Requirements Reagents used to perform the tests must be FDA cleared, as appropriate, or be identified as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT). Offerors of tests not in compliance with these requirements shall not be considered for award under this solicitation. New Items vs. Refurbished or Grey Market Goods This solicitation is for the award of new items only. The Contractor shall provide only new equipment and new parts for the required products described herein. Absolutely no grey market goods or refurbished products shall be provided under any delivery order. Grey market goods are defined as genuine branded goods sold outside of an authorized sales-territory (or by non-authorized dealers in an authorized territory) at prices lower than being charged in authorized sales territories (or by authorized dealers). All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer s warranty. Trade Agreements Act The Trade Agreements Act is applicable to all Schedules. In exercising its authority under FAR Part 25, Foreign Acquisition, purchases by Ordering Activities are restricted to either U.S.-made or designated country end products as defined in clause FAR 52.225-5. For the purposes of this services schedule, origin is determined by the country in which the firm providing the service is established, not the location at which the services are performed. title: Firefox
description: UPDATE: The purpose of Amendment 1 to DARPA-PA-26-137, the Firefox Program Solicitation (PS), is to update the deadlines for OPP submissions and presentations. The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) has developed a non-invasive coherent optical system capable of recording neural signals in humans. To expand this foundational technology and enable the development of revolutionary, non-invasive brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), DARPA's Firefox program is soliciting approaches to overcome key technological hurdles: 1) development of components enabling dynamic rastering/scanning of the incoming coherent optical signal to target multiple regions of interest and 2) development of new data processing architectures beyond the digital domain to handle the high data rates and computational burden inherent to scaling the amount of neural data recorded by the optical system. The ultimate goal of the Firefox program is to use these innovations to develop a 100-channel, non-invasive BCI with 50-micron spatial and 100-microsecond temporal resolution.
